description: We are a passionate group of innovators who love building software projects and expressing creativity. Our team thrives at the intersection of technology and imagination, blending problem‑solving with artistic vision to craft impactful solutions. Together, we aim to push boundaries, turn ideas into reality, and contribute meaningfully to the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
We developed MARGIN, an offline-first, browser-based space mission design game and simulation platform where players conceptualize, engineer, launch and operate authentic interplanetary missions.

Addressing the NASA Space Apps Challenge, MARGIN models the full mission lifecycle across authentic flight regimes—spanning Low Earth Orbit, Lunar polar landing, Mars exploration and roving, and asteroid sample return at Bennu. Grounded entirely in authoritative NASA and JPL datasets (including DE440/441 Chebyshev ephemerides, LSP launch vehicle curves, LRO LOLA and MRO HiRISE terrain grids, and 19 flight-heritage instruments), players balance five strict margin rails: mass, power, comms link budget, financial cost, and schedule. It features interactive Lambert porkchop solvers, stochastic in-flight anomalies, and solo or 2–4 player role-gated team collaboration with unanimous pre-flight roll-calls.

This project is vital because space systems engineering is governed by competing trade-offs that students rarely experience as an interconnected system. MARGIN bridges theory with practice, providing transparent cause-and-effect post-mission diagnostics that show exactly how early engineering decisions shaped mission survival.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

MARGIN (Mission Architecture & Resource Generation Interface for NASA) is an offline-first, browser-based space mission design game and systems engineering simulator. It guides players through the full lifecycle of an interplanetary mission—from concept to surface exploration—across six flight regimes (Low Earth Orbit, Lunar polar landing, Mars exploration and roving, asteroid sample return at Bennu, Jovian icy moon flybys, and unconstrained Sandboxes).

Powered by an authoritative simulation engine (derive(S) in game.js), MARGIN couples aerospace equations across five strict margin rails: Mass, Power, Comms Link, Budget Cap, and Schedule. The operational loop follows six chronological phases:

Formulation & Science Objectives: Select mission priorities (mineralogy, volatiles, magnetic fields, atmosphere) with explicit data volume and weight targets.

Spacecraft Systems Engineering: Configure payloads from 19 flight-heritage instruments (HiRISE, OCI, OVIRS, REASON, SAM) and engineer supporting bus systems (solar arrays vs. MMRTG, eclipse batteries, X/Ka-band antennas, chemical/ion propulsion, radiation vaults).

Trajectory & Launch Selection: Scrub departure windows on an interactive Lambert porkchop plot (trading C3, flight time, arrival V_inf) and match wet mass against NASA Launch Services Program (LSP) performance curves across 9 real rockets (Falcon 9/Heavy, Atlas V, Vulcan, New Glenn, SLS Block 1B, Saturn V).

Flight Readiness Review & Launch: Clear five mandatory FRR safety gates, triggering an authentic launch ascent with multi-stage separation physics.

Cruise Operations & In-Flight Anomalies: Planetary bodies propagate along vendored JPL DE440/DE441 Chebyshev state vectors. Players navigate time-warp, manage Deep Space Network (DSN) passes, handle 1/r^2 solar power decay, and mitigate stochastic anomalies (solar particle events, thruster degradation, DSN outages).

Planetary Surface Operations: Landed missions transition into 3D dioramas generated from NASA PDS LRO LOLA (Moon) and MRO HiRISE / MGS MOLA (Mars Jezero Crater) elevation models, commanding NASA RASSOR and Perseverance rovers across real slope, hazard, and comms geometries.

Post-Mission Graded Report: Runs conclude with an exhaustive debrief featuring letter grades, cause-and-effect failure diagnostics, and direct benchmarking against historical NASA missions (PACE, LRO, MRO, OSIRIS-REx, Europa Clipper).

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

Space Exploration for Everyone (Learning Through Play): You don't need a degree in aerospace engineering to design an interplanetary mission. MARGIN transforms complex physics into an intuitive, thrilling game where anyone can learn through hands-on experimentation. By tinkering with real instruments, rockets, and orbits, players discover firsthand how space missions work—turning abstract science into an entertaining, curiosity-driven adventure for students, gamers, families, and space enthusiasts of all ages.

Universal Accessibility (Zero Barriers): Quality STEM education should be fun and open to all. MARGIN runs 100% offline directly in any standard browser—requiring no installations, high-end gaming hardware, or paid software licenses. Whether on a school Chromebook, a tablet, or an older family laptop with limited internet, anyone in the world can instantly step into the shoes of a NASA flight director.

Social & Collaborative Entertainment: Real space exploration is the ultimate team effort. With built-in hot-seat multiplayer for 1 to 4 players, friends, classmates, or families can team up across authentic NASA roles (Flight Director, Science Lead, Spacecraft Engineer, Comms/Nav Lead), debating priorities, solving surprise in-flight anomalies, and celebrating unanimous "GO FOR LAUNCH" moments together.

3. Tools, Languages & Technical Architecture

Core Architecture: Authored in clean Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, and CSS3 without frameworks, bundlers, or external CDNs.

3D Graphics & Shaders: Built with Three.js (r160) and custom GLSL shaders (photosphere limb darkening, atmospheric limb shells, volumetric exhaust cones, terrain normal drapes).

Scientific Data Pipeline: Evaluates vendored NASA/JPL DE440/DE441 Chebyshev ephemerides, NASA PDS Bennu radar mesh (DOI: 10.26033/33ba-s419), LRO LOLA lunar elevation grids, and MRO HiRISE stereo DTMs locally.

3D Compression & Assets: Uses Google Draco WASM decoding for official NASA 3D models (Mobile Launcher, Perseverance, RASSOR, Apollo LM, Satellite Kit modular bus).

Audio Engineering: Web Audio API synthesizing authentic Apollo MSFN Quindar tones (2525 Hz / 2475 Hz) and tactile relay clicks, layered with NASA JSC launch acoustics and an ambient score generated via Google Flow Music (Lyria 3.5).

Progressive Enhancement: Features an independent Canvas2D fallback rendering path running identically under file:// or ?no3d.

4. Creativity & Team Considerations

"Margin" as Gameplay: Transforming engineering margins from static spreadsheets into dynamic visual safety rails that react instantly to player choices.

Dual-Tier Scaffolding: Balancing accessibility for beginners via Cadet Mode (subsidized margins, auto-recommendations, 28-term glossary) with deep rigor in Flight Director Mode (unforgiving limits, realistic DSN blackouts).

Scientific Provenance Firewall: Clearly separating real NASA/JPL data from gameplay abstractions through an interactive in-game NASA Provenance modal.
